claims.statement: Per-user preferences are stored in exactly one nullable JSON column, `UserModel.preferences` on `auth_users`, added by the Alembic revision 1548d7b88af5 and mirrored as `UserSchema.preferences`; there is one document per user and nothing is keyed by security, route, or device.

The preferences surface is GET, PUT and PATCH on `/accounts/me/preferences`, mounted under `/api/v1` by `src/main.py`; GET returns `{}` when nothing is saved, and all three endpoints depend on `current_user` so an unauthenticated request returns 401.

The request payload model `UserPreferences` in `src/account/api_types.py` uses `model_config = ConfigDict(extra="allow")` and declares a different key set from the frontend `UserPreferences` interface: `watchlist_sort` exists only on the backend model, while `sidebar_watchlists`, `collapsed_watchlist_ids`, `expanded_account_ids`, `drawings`, `holdings_table`, `holdings_group` and `indicator_pane_heights` exist only on the frontend, and `display_currency` is the one key declared on both sides with a validator on the backend. Unknown keys therefore round-trip through storage unchanged while declared fields are still type-validated, so neither declaration is authoritative and both must be read together to inventory the keys.

Both write verbs dump with `exclude_none=True`, so an explicit JSON null is never persisted and cannot clear a stored key: PUT replaces the whole document (a partial PUT body is a replace, not a merge), while PATCH can only add or overwrite non-null top-level keys.

PATCH performs a top-level-only merge by assigning `coalesce(cast(preferences, JSONB), cast({}, JSONB)).op("||")(cast(payload, JSONB))` with `RETURNING preferences`, which makes nested objects such as `indicators`, `wave_settings`, `elliott_waves` and `holdings_table` whole-value keys and makes one-key-per-write the race-safe shape for independently mounted components.

Persistence failure handling differs per surface: layout and sidebar writes are fire-and-forget (`patchPreferences(...).catch(console.error)`), the `/holdings` page captures rejections into a page-level `persistError` rendered in a destructive alert, the `/watchlists` reorder path rolls the optimistic order back and sets `watchlistService.error`, and the security page and `ChartDrawingsService` writes only log.

`ChartDrawingsService` is the only writer of the `elliott_waves`, `fibonacci_tools` and `drawings` keys, patching them from wave/fib/drawing change handlers, the undo/redo restore path and the deferred drag-end flush, and it reads them back through per-security getters keyed by security id.

Two declared preference keys have no consumer: `sidebar_watchlists` exists only in the frontend interface, and `watchlist_sort` is declared on the backend model and covered by a router test but is not read by any frontend code, because per-watchlist security sort moved to the `WatchlistRead.sort` column persisted through `PATCH /market/watchlists/{id}`.

`mergeChartPreferences` in `frontend/src/lib/chart-preferences.ts` is a tested read-merge-write helper that preserves the `indicators` key across partial writes, but no production code calls it: the security page's `updateChartPreferences` issues a bare partial PATCH and relies on the server's top-level merge.

Because `extra="allow"` lets unvalidated values into the column, robustness lives in the readers: `normalizeHoldingsTableConfig` drops unknown column ids, clamps widths to per-column bounds and forces the sticky first column visible, `normalizeHoldingsGroupMode` maps anything that is not `stock`/`company` to `'none'`, and `holdings-modal.svelte` rejects a stored `holdings_period` outside its `PERIODS` list in favour of `ALL`.

Per-security indicator preferences were removed in favour of the user-global `indicators` key: the `market_indicator_preferences` table and its `GET|PUT /market/securities/{id}/indicator-preferences` endpoints are gone, and a regression test asserts those routes return 404.

Whole-key writers always send the complete value because a PATCH replaces the key: `handlePaneHeightsChange` sends the full pane-height map (or null), `handleWaveSettingsChange` sends the whole settings object, and `IndicatorsGroup` sends the entire `indicators` map on toggle, settings save and reset.

A failed preferences read is never fatal and is load-bearing for wave alerts: the security page leaves its `userPreferences` state at the `null` sentinel when the fetch rejects, and the initial wave-alert reconcile in the post-navigation effect is gated on `userPreferences !== null`, so a preference outage cannot mass-delete wave-target alerts.
`holdings_period` is read by `holdings-modal.svelte` on every modal open (not by the route loads) and written by the period selector through a fire-and-forget patch that only logs failures.

`tests/routers/test_accounts.py` is the backend contract test suite for preferences: it pins the empty-document response, PUT/GET round-trip, partial-update-without-fabricated-defaults, cross-component PATCH isolation, per-user isolation in both directions, per-key round-trips for `sidebar_open`, `holdings_period`, `elliott_waves`, `fibonacci_tools`, `wave_settings` and `watchlist_order`/`watchlist_sort`, and the `display_currency` normalize-and-reject cases for both PUT and PATCH.

`UserPreferencesService` in `frontend/src/lib/api/userPreferencesService.ts` is the only client of `/accounts/me/preferences`, extending `ApiClient` with `getPreferences`, `savePreferences` (PUT) and `patchPreferences` (PATCH). It is exported as `getUserPreferencesService(customFetch)` for SSR loads that inject the server `fetch` and pass the `auth_token` cookie via the token override, and as a module singleton `userPreferencesService` for browser components; the two holdings helpers instead accept a minimal structural `{ getPreferences, patchPreferences }` service so tests can inject a double.

The root layout load (`frontend/src/routes/+layout.server.ts`) reads exactly `sidebar_open`, `collapsed_watchlist_ids`, `watchlist_order` and `expanded_account_ids` on every authenticated request, guarding each with a per-key type check (`typeof ... === 'boolean'` / `Array.isArray(...)`) and defaulting to `true`, `[]`, `null` and `[]`; the read is skipped when `locals.user` is unset and any request failure is swallowed so layout hydration never fails on a preferences outage.

The `/holdings` server load reads `holdings_table`, `holdings_group` and `elliott_waves` as one of three parallel `Promise.allSettled` requests (with portfolios and accounts) and treats a preferences failure as non-fatal, returning `normalizeHoldingsTableConfig(null)`, `normalizeHoldingsGroupMode(null)` (`'none'`) and `null` waves while the load still returns; a 401 `ApiError` from any of the three services instead deletes the auth cookie and throws a 303 redirect to `/auth/login?clear_session=true`. The `/watchlists` load reads no preference at all (returning `{ watchlists: [] }`, with the page seeding `watchlistOrder` from `$page.data.watchlist_order`) and the security route load returns only `security_id`, with the page fetching preferences client-side after navigation.

The security page is the only component that caches the whole preferences document: it holds it in `userPreferences`, re-reads `show_valuation_band` and calls `applySavedPaneHeights` on both the initial load and the post-navigation fetch, and forwards the document to `ChartDrawingsService.setPreferences`, which keeps the drawing keys `elliott_waves`, `fibonacci_tools` and `drawings`; `IndicatorsGroup.loadPreferences` independently fetches the same document and republishes it through `onPreferencesLoaded`.

The key `expanded_account_ids` is owned end-to-end by the accounts list: the root layout load publishes it as page data, `AccountsList` seeds a `SvelteSet` from context or `$page.data` and republishes it under the `expandedAccountIds` context, and `AccountsListItem` resolves its initial expansion with precedence `initialExpanded` prop → context set → context initial list → `$page.data`, patching the whole array fire-and-forget on every caret toggle.

`show_valuation_band` is written by a different component than the one that reads it: `fundamentals-group.svelte`'s overlay checkbox patches it in the actions sidebar (logging failures only), while the security page applies it to the chart's `showValuationOverlay` state, so the two never share component state.

`collapsed_watchlist_ids` is written whole-array and fire-and-forget by `AppSidebarWatchlist.toggleCollapsed`, which reads the initial set with precedence context value → `$page.data.collapsed_watchlist_ids` → empty.

Write-failure handling is split by surface: layout/sidebar/account-card writes are fire-and-forget (`.catch(console.error)`) and never block the interaction; `/holdings` surfaces failures through `persist(promise, fallbackMessage)`, which sets `persistError` and renders it via `errorMessage = persistError ?? service.errorMessage`; `/watchlists` rolls the optimistic reorder back before setting `watchlistService.error`; and every security-page, `IndicatorsGroup`, `holding-group`, `holdings-modal` and `ChartDrawingsService` write only logs.

Reading unvalidated stored values is each consumer's responsibility, not a server-side guarantee: `normalizeHoldingsTableConfig` drops unknown columns and clamps widths, `normalizeHoldingsGroupMode` maps anything other than `stock`/`company` to `'none'`, and `holdings-modal.svelte` rejects a stored `holdings_period` outside `PERIODS` in favour of `ALL`; `loadHoldingsTableConfig`/`loadHoldingsGroupMode` additionally tolerate thrown requests and never write on load.

`display_currency` is the only preference key validated on the way in: a `mode="before"` field validator on the backend `UserPreferences` trims and upper-cases the value and rejects anything outside `SUPPORTED_DISPLAY_CURRENCIES` (CAD, USD, EUR, GBP) with a 422 that stores nothing, for both PUT and PATCH; the supported set is declared twice — the Python tuple in `src/account/api_types.py` and the frontend `SUPPORTED_DISPLAY_CURRENCIES` / `DisplayCurrency` that feeds the settings select — so both declarations must change together.

`display_currency` is the only preference with a server-side consumer: `UserApi.get_display_currency` returns the stored string when it is a non-empty string and `CAD` otherwise, and `GET /accounts/holdings` and `GET /accounts/holdings/{security_id}` pass it to `PositionService` as the conversion target for every returned row, so the effective value changes holdings totals without any client-side currency logic.

`/settings/preferences` owns the display-currency UI and fails closed on the read: its server load reads the document with the `auth_token` cookie and returns `display_currency` defaulting to `CAD`, deleting the cookie and redirecting to `/auth/login?clear_session=true` on a missing token or 401 and raising `error(status, message)` on any other `ApiError`; the page then patches `{ display_currency }` on select change, adopts the server-normalized value from the response, and on rejection restores the previous value in both state and the select element while rendering the message in a destructive alert.

After the holdings-service refactor the `/holdings` page reads no preferences client-side: it seeds its page-owned `HoldingsService` with `data.group_mode` and its `tableConfig` with `normalizeHoldingsTableConfig(data.holdings_table_config)` from the server load, and its only preference traffic is outbound single-key patches (`saveHoldingsGroupMode` / `saveHoldingsTableConfig`) wrapped in `persist(...)`, which leaves `loadHoldingsTableConfig` / `loadHoldingsGroupMode` without a production caller.

Adding a key inside the existing JSON document needs no Alembic revision — `display_currency` and the holdings/drawing keys shipped without one, and the feature's only revision is `1548d7b88af5`, which created the nullable `preferences` JSON column on `auth_users` — whereas changing that column or adding a real table column still requires the model change plus its migration in the same change.
